transcript:
Header:
Date: 2029-04-02
Start: 15:00 PT | Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Avery Collins (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Morales (Riverbend Head of IT), Priya Singh (Riverbend Security Architect), Dr. Ethan Browne (Clinical Informatics)

Auto-generated Summary: (may be rough)
- Discussed pilot scope for Riverbend Health; primary focus on security and compliance controls for a limited pilot serving de-identified clinical notes and triage assistant.
- Agreed on success criteria + benchmarks and action items to share docs and plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Avery from Redwood, joining with Samir our SE, thanks for doing this, Lena, Priya, Ethan, how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Lena: Good, good, thanks. We wanted to make sure we can go deep on security items, we have some internal checklist items around SOC two, ISO 27001, SSO, RBAC, audit logging, things like that.
[00:20] Samir: Yep totally, that's what we usually scope for health pilots. We'll go through success criteria, then do sizing and benchmarks, and then the specific compliance asks.
[01:02] Priya: Quick note, we're only doing a small pilot initially — about 10k users internally, maybe 50 concurrent sessions at peak, so it's not big but security is non-negotiable.
[01:15] Avery: Great, makes sense. Can you confirm what data class you'll be sending? de-id or PHI?
[01:22] Dr. Ethan: For the pilot we'll only send de-identified clinical notes and synthetic messages. We want to test the workflow and latency, not PHI exposure yet.
[01:35] Lena: We'll also want to validate audit trail and retention, for our SOPs it needs 1 year immutable logs for the pilot, and 7 years if we roll to production.
[01:50] Samir: Noted. For success criteria, here's what we typically recommend: end-to-end 95th percentile latency under 800ms for single-turn prompts, throughput to handle sustained 50 qps with 2x burst, and model output quality matching our eval prompts — we'll provide a rubric.
[02:20] Priya: The latency target is okay, but we need clarity on tail latency. Also encryption at rest and in-transit, and KMS integration for key control.
[02:35] Avery: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations in Private deployments and Dedicated as well, and for hosted we can support envelope encryption and bring-your-own-KMS in certain tiers — though for pilot we recommend Dedicated or Private if you need KMS control.
[02:58] Lena: We're evaluating Dedicated vs Private — Dedicated if we can get VPC peering and strict network controls, Private if we need the control plane in our VPC.
[03:14] Samir: Right, Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools and predictable throughput; Private is full customer-managed control plane. For a pilot, many customers do a Dedicated reserved pool in a customer project with VPC peering.
[03:30] Dr. Ethan: On workload sizing: typical prompt is ~350 tokens, average 2.5 calls per session, estimate 100k tokens/day during pilot, peaking at 1M tokens/day for heavier tests — does that line up with your throughput planning?
[03:50] Samir: Yes, that maps. If average prompt+response is 350 tokens times QPS, we can calculate RPS and token throughput. For 50 concurrent sessions with 2.5 calls each over an hour, we will recommend a benchmark window. We'll share a sizing spreadsheet.
[04:12] Priya: Audit logs. We need field-level auditability: user ID, request payload hash, model version, response hash, timestamp, and operator id. Logs must be immutable and stored for at least one year for pilot.
[04:29] Avery: We can produce audit logs with those fields in Dedicated and Private; for hosted we provide logs but the retention and immutability varies by plan — we'll include the exact schema in the security pack.
[05:03] Lena: SSO — we run Okta, want SAML-based SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Can you handle SAML and role mappings?
[05:15] Samir: Yes, Redwood supports SSO via SAML, and SCIM for user sync. RBAC is configurable — we can map Okta groups to Redwood roles, down to route-level permissions. We'll need a test IdP to validate.
[05:38] Priya: Also want to limit which models are accessible to pilot users. Need model allow-lists and canary rollouts.
[05:47] Samir: We have model pinning and rollout controls in the console. You can restrict a role to only call certain models and versions.
[06:10] Dr. Ethan: Benchmarking — we want a benchmark run that exercises sequence lengths to replicate triage: some short prompts (~50 tokens), some medium (~350), and long (~1,200). Can you run latency and throughput tests and share token-level cost?
[06:30] Avery: Absolutely. Samir will propose a benchmark plan with specific payloads and a test window. We'll run both steady-state and spike tests and provide per-token latency breakdowns.
[06:45] Samir: For the plan, we'll need a test environment — ideally a Dedicated pool or Private node, to mirror production. We'll run tests at 10k, 50k, 100k token/sec levels depending on scope. Also will include KV cache and batching configs.
[07:10] Priya: For security we need SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestation. Can you share your most recent reports and any penetration test summaries?
[07:25] Avery: Yes, we'll send SOC 2 and ISO certs and a redacted pen test summary. For pilot, many customers accept SOC 2 + encryptions + RBAC; if you need dedicated SOC attestations we can escalate.
[07:45] Lena: Data residency — pilot will be US-only, but regional controls matter. We want assurances data won't cross regions.
[07:56] Samir: We'll confirm region placement and routing policy; Dedicated pools can be pinned to a region and we have smart routing options.
[08:12] Dr. Ethan: What about data deletion and retention? If we need to purge pilot data after tests, how quick is that?
[08:21] Avery: For Dedicated and Private we support on-request data purges and configurable retention; for hosted there are standard retention windows. We'll document timelines in the security pack.
[08:42] Priya: RBAC specifics: need at least three roles for pilot — admin (full), operator (run benchmarks, view logs), reader (view-only). Also need approval workflow for granting operator role.
[09:00] Samir: That's straightforward; our console supports role templates and you can create custom roles. Approval workflow we can integrate with Okta/approval workflows but might require an integration via SCIM + webhook. We'll note that as an integration item.
[09:28] Avery: On timelines — customer hoping for a 6-week pilot: week 1 setup and SSO, week 2 baseline benchmark, week 3 adjustments, week 4-5 extended tests with clinical prompts, week 6 review and decision. Is that feasible?
[09:45] Lena: 6 weeks is tight but doable if we get docs quickly. We need SOC 2 + network diagram passed to internal security by week 1.
[09:58] Priya: We'll also require a short threat model review before onboarding.
[10:05] Samir: We can do a 30-minute threat model call after you review the docs.
[10:22] Dr. Ethan: Success criteria recap: 95p latency under 800ms, 99p under 2s for typical prompt distribution, throughput to handle 50 qps sustained with 2x burst, acceptable output quality measured by our rubric, and audit/SSO/RBAC controls validated.
[10:45] Avery: Good, we'll put that in the pilot charter.
[11:05] Lena: A few technical questions: will the KV cache persist between requests in your Dedicated runtime? We rely on session context.
[11:15] Samir: Yes, we maintain KV cache per session and we can configure cache TTLs. Some of the infra terms in the transcript might be misheard — KV cache was sometimes transcribed as KV cash in older notes — but yes it's KV cache.
[11:40] Priya: Any multi-tenancy concerns? We need to ensure tenant isolation at the network and process level.
[11:50] Samir: Dedicated gives you isolated pools; Private is fully customer-managed. We'll include diagrams showing process boundaries and network ACLs.
[12:08] Dr. Ethan: For regression testing, we need model version pinning and drift detection.
[12:18] Avery: Redwood Optimize can run evals and regression alerts tied to a test set; for pilot we can configure lightweight checks.
[12:33] Lena: About costs — we'll need a cost estimate for pilot (tokens, reserved capacity if Dedicated).
[12:41] Avery: We'll send a pilot cost worksheet with estimated tokens and a Dedicated reservation option for the 6-week window.
[12:55] Priya: On audit logs again — we prefer logs to be delivered to our SIEM via syslog or S3 with write-once settings. Is that supported?
[13:05] Samir: Yes, we can push logs to S3, and many customers use S3 with Object Lock for write-once. Also direct SIEM integration via syslog or event broker is available in Dedicated/Private.
[13:30] Lena: Can you provide a sample of the log schema and a few example entries?
[13:37] Avery: We'll include a sample schema in the security pack.
[13:50] Dr. Ethan: Any red flags we should be aware of from your side?
[13:56] Samir: Nothing major — small items like SSO test user creation and firewall rules need coordination. Also we'll want a narrow test window for benchmarks to avoid production interference.
[14:10] Priya: Regarding SAML, we want signed assertions and authncontext enforcement.
[14:18] Samir: We support signed assertions and can request specific authncontext levels.
[14:30] Avery: Ok, let's capture action items and next steps.
[14:35] Lena: Quick note: our legal team wants to look at data processing addendum and standard contractual clauses if data goes to non-US regions — but pilot is US only so that's lower priority for now.
[14:50] Priya: Also will need proof of penetration testing within last 12 months.
[14:57] Avery: We'll include a redacted pen test summary.
[15:10] Samir: For benchmarks I'll propose three phases: baseline (single-node), load (steady-state target qps), and spike (2-3x burst). We'll provide the scripts and help run them.
[15:25] Dr. Ethan: Sounds good. For acceptance criteria last item is a simple user acceptance test (UAT) where clinicians run the triage flow against the system and we review responses for safety and accuracy.
[15:42] Lena: Ok, schedule wise — please send docs by Friday and we'll target SSO setup next Tuesday.
[15:50] Avery: Will do. Anything else?
[15:55] Priya: Just to reiterate, audit log retention, KMS control, SAML and RBAC are mandatory for pilot.
[16:05] Avery: Understood. We'll mark them must-haves in the pilot charter and include them in the security pack.
[16:12] Samir: I'll follow up with benchmark spreadsheet and test plan.
[16:18] Lena: Thanks everyone, appreciate it.
[16:21] Avery: Thanks, we'll follow up with docs and scheduling.

(Transcription notes: occasional mis-hearings: "KV cash" -> KV cache; "Redwood Dedicate" -> Redwood Dedicated; punctuation and names may be slightly off)
notes: Pilot charter to include must-have security items: SOC 2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, immutable audit logs, KMS integration, region pinning
